title: Fold a receptacle's stiff copper conductors into its wall box, seat it flush and drive both mounting screws
instruction: Mount the outlet in its wall box: every wire inside the box, the outlet flush on the wall and both of its mounting screws driven in.
context: Electricians (821,000 US jobs, BLS 2025; O*NET 47-2111.00: "Assemble, install, test, or maintain electrical or electronic wiring, equipment, appliances, apparatus, or fixtures") finish every receptacle this way; the maker's instructions say to fold the wires into the box and screw the receptacle to it. Solid 14 AWG copper keeps its bends and pushes back, so the outlet stalls short of the wall: one hand must hold it in, square and on the screw holes' line, while the other drives each screw until it catches.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, on the table: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table. Wall (fixed): 1/2 in. (1.27 cm) gypsum board 26 x 20 cm standing on the table, face at x 32, from y -17 to y +9, on a 2x4 stud (3.8 x 8.9 cm) right of the box and a 2x4 plate. Box (fixed): Carlon B120A one-gang PVC nail-on box, blue, 5.7 wide x 9.8 tall x 8.3 deep outside, 3 mm walls, rim flush with the wall's face, opening centred at y -4, 11 up; two screw bosses inside on its vertical centre line, holes 8.33 apart. Cable: 14/2 NM-B stub entering the box's bottom back. Conductors: solid 14 AWG copper (1.63 mm), black and white insulated to 2.8 mm, 19.4 cm from the cable to their terminals; bare 19.5 cm. Receptacle (loose, 45 g): 15 A duplex, ivory, strap 10.7 tall x 2.2 wide, body 6.7 x 3.3 x 2.0, face 0.4 thick; black on its brass screw (robot's right), white on its silver screw (left), bare on its green screw; two captive 6-32 mounting screws standing 1.7 out behind the strap. It hangs on its conductors, upright, facing the robot, strap 8 in front of the wall, centre about 5 mm above the opening's centre; the conductors arch from the cable up to about 3.7 above the opening's centre and down to the terminals (wire_start_points.csv). Not connected to power. Driver (loose, 0.31 kg): Bosch GO class push-to-start cordless screwdriver, 19 x 4 x 4 cm with a #2 bit, lying on its side pointing at the wall, centred at x 24, y -21.5. Distractors (loose, ignored by the scorer): lineman's pliers (19 cm, 0.32 kg) at x 6, y 24, and long-nose pliers (23.5 cm, 0.18 kg) at x 20, y 30, flat, handles toward the robot.
scoring: Judged each step from the end state. In place: no point of any conductor more than 1.0 mm in front of the wall's face, every fingertip of both grippers at least 3 cm from the receptacle and every conductor, and the driver's bit at least 2 cm from the receptacle. 0: not in place, or no mounting screw driven home. 0.25: in place, one screw home. 0.5: in place, both screws home, but the strap more than 1.0 mm off the wall at either screw or the face more than 3 degrees off square. 1.0: in place, both screws home, strap within 1.0 mm of the wall at both screws and square within 3 degrees, receptacle moving under 5 mm/s, all held 1 s. A screw is home once its thread has drawn the strap to the wall at that screw; screws cannot be backed out. The score is the last step's, or 1.0 once the 1.0 row has held 1 s.
reset_notes: Fresh conductor every trial (cut the 14/2 cable stub new, strip 16 mm, land black, white and bare), so the copper starts annealed; back both screws out first. About 5 minutes. The cable is never connected to power.
fidelity: Conductors are chains of 12 mm rigid links on two-axis joints, elastic-plastic per joint from copper's 117 GPa modulus and 69 MPa yield with estimated hardening; no twist, insulation stiffness left out. Screw threads are computed: a running bit on a head whose tip is in the boss hole draws the strap in 0.79 mm per turn (force capped at 60 N). Receptacle, box, wall and driver are rigid primitives at true size; the driver's push-start spindle is a sprung slider.
